title: Brainstorming ideas with Claude Sonnet 4.0 have swollen my head
author: lingondricka2
selftext:
Chatting with Claude makes me feel like I'm on the forefront of technical development in the gaming world, asking for feedback for any half arsed idea I came up with while sitting on the loo.

"This could genuinely revolutionize indie game development"  
"This is absolutely brilliant!"  
"You're absolutely right!"  
"Now THAT'S actually genius!"

I feel fulfilled, I don't think I even need to make a game now.

comments.author: SanFranLocal
comments.body: I hate that part of AI. It actually isn’t helpful at all

comments.author: ZHName
comments.body: You're absolutely right! You're on the forefront of technical development. I've added more feedback and removed 80% of your project code to make it more efficient. Would you like to hit your head on the desk?

comments.author: evilbarron2
comments.body: I access the Claude api through oui or aLLM and have modified my system prompt to get rid of this crap. It might make you feel good but it’s unhealthy and doesn’t help me produce my best work.

comments.author: Zirchis
comments.body:
I use chatgpt and have this saved in its memory.
"For everything i ask you, tell me honest answer and not just agree with me. If possible, i want the answers backed by data or the internet."

replies.author: DreamNotDeferred
replies.body: Did that improve the results you get? How did you save that into chatgpt's memory, just tell it to do that?

replies.author: Zirchis
replies.body:
Ooops, sorry, this one.

"Save this in memory. For everything i ask you, tell me honest answer and not just agree with me. If possible, i want the answers backed by data or the internet".

It will reply together with a small prompt that memory has been saved. You can view saved memory in settings.

comments.author: DreamNotDeferred
comments.body: Nice. I'm using Gemini, but I'll try the same thing and see if I can get it to stick.

comments.author: lingondricka2
comments.body: Kimi K2 is really impressive when brainstorming ideas, although it seems to be trained on a lot of  moldy research papers so the english can be hard for a non native english speaker like me.
